Today, the Problem Solvers Caucus Co-Chairs @RepBrianFitz and @RepTomSuozzi announced the formation of a new bipartisan working group focused on artificial intelligence and evolving technologies.

The working group will be led by @RepJoshG and @RepMikeLawler with @RepScholten and @RepBlakeMoore serving as vice leads.

On this date in 1787, delegates to the Constitutional Convention signed a document creating a government by, of and for the people. 

As Benjamin Franklin left Independence Hall, Elizabeth Willing Powell asked him, “Well, Doctor, what have we got — a Republic or a Monarchy?”

Franklin responded, “A Republic, if you can keep it.” 

I swore an oath to preserve, protect and defend the U.S. Constitution. With an Administration that too often ignores or violates the limits on government and the rights of the people established in that document, and Congressional Republicans who refuse to serve as a check on these impulses, it is up to each and every American to ensure we keep it.

text:
On this Constitution Day I reflect on the words of Benjamin Franklin after the Constitutional Convention in 1787,  Franklin said of the constitution, the document was not flawless, stating he agreed to it "with all its faults" because he doubted any convention could make a better one.

Recognizing their own limitations, the Framers included Article V to establish a clear process for adding amendments, allowing future generations to correct mistakes and adapt the framework.

The Preamble uses the phrase "a more perfect union," reflecting the Framers' understanding that government is an ongoing project meant to be continuously improved.

Today we honor that history and continue our quest toward that “more perfect union.”

New World screwworm is a serious threat to livestock, wildlife, and the agricultural economy in South Texas.

I met with Dr. Ian Simon of @FlyttrGlobal to discuss the current outbreak and the work they are doing in San Antonio to develop new tools to help stop its spread.

Flyttr is working with Texas Biomed on next-generation biological solutions that build on proven methods like the Sterile Insect Technique. We discussed how new technology can support the broader federal response and help protect ranchers and producers across Texas.

I will continue working with USDA, researchers, and the private sector to strengthen our response to New World screwworm and protect South Texas agriculture.

Having sworn an oath to support and defend this sacred document, I’m committed to upholding its vision and promise - and the clear separation of powers - that our Founders envisioned.

text:
Students from migrant and seasonal farmworker families should have the opportunity to finish their education and continue on to college.

I spoke with leaders from the National HEP/CAMP Association about the High School Equivalency Program and College Assistance Migrant Program and the students they serve.

HEP helps farmworkers and their families earn a high school equivalency credential and take the next step toward a job or higher education. CAMP helps students from farmworker families succeed during their first year of college.

I have supported federal funding for these programs through the appropriations process because they give students another pathway to build a better future for themselves and their families. 

I will continue working to support educational opportunities for students in South Texas and across the country.

I met with cotton producers and representatives from Plains Cotton Growers and the Arizona Cotton Growers Association to discuss the issues facing farmers across Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas, and Arizona.

Cotton producers are dealing with high input costs, market uncertainty, weather challenges, and tight margins. They need a strong farm safety net, a farm bill that gives producers certainty, and policies that support American-grown cotton.

I voted for the Farm, Food, and National Security Act, and I am a cosponsor of the Buying American Cotton Act, which supports U.S.-grown cotton and domestic textile production.

I will continue working with agriculture leaders to support producers, strengthen rural communities, and protect the farmers who help feed and clothe our country.

As a former prosecutor and now in Congress, I know that real public safety means addressing the root causes of crime through evidence-based diversion, addiction and mental health treatment. It also means investing in community-partnered violence reduction rather than over-incarceration.

I was honored to share the stage and hear insights from some of the folks leading the charge in their communities:
Dr. Shawanna Vaughn, Founder of Silent Cry
Dr. Luke Wood, President of Sacramento State
Dr. Kendra Holmes, President & CEO of Affinia Healthcare
Dr. Topeka K. Sam, Founder of The Ladies of Hope Ministries

Families in San Diego wouldn’t skip fixing their roof if it meant they had to pay three times more when a storm hits. But that's how Congress budgets health care: look at the costs of care in the short-term instead of decades from now. 

That's the blind spot my bipartisan Preventive Health Savings Act fixes, and I was glad it unanimously passed the Budget Committee this week so that Congress can better asses how today's decisions impact patients and reduce health care costs in the future.

Local franchise owners need clear federal rules so they can hire workers, follow the law, and operate their businesses.

I will continue working to support small businesses, support local jobs, and make sure employers in South Texas have the certainty they need to operate and grow.

text:
The war in Iran is driving up costs for American families.

A new analysis from the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office estimates the war has already cost taxpayers roughly $40 billion and contributed to higher inflation. CBO projects it could raise inflation by another 0.5 percentage points in early 2027, largely because of higher energy prices.

Higher energy prices mean higher costs for gas, transportation, utilities, food and other everyday expenses. Americans have already spent an additional $71.5 billion on gas since the war began, an average of $604 per family.

American families shouldn’t have to keep paying more at the pump and at the grocery store. I’ll continue working to protect taxpayers and make sure federal spending is responsible and accountable.

ROAD TO 250: The Road to Independence 

“We the People.”

On September 17, 1787, after months of debate and compromise, delegates in Philadelphia signed the United States Constitution, establishing the framework of government that still guides our nation today.

The Constitution was never meant to end our debates. It gave us a way to have them, through representative government, checks and balances, and a system designed to endure even when we disagree.

As we continue to celebrate America’s 250th, Constitution Day is a good reminder that our democracy depends not only on the words written on that parchment, but on each generation doing its part to uphold them.

Today I led PA House Dems in pressing ICE, GEO, and Clearfield County, Pennsylvania, for transparency on the use of taxpayer dollars to fund the private prison company that runs Moshannon Valley Processing Center, the largest detention center in the Northeast.

The private prison company has reported record profits driven by this Administration’s mass deportation and immigrant surveillance campaigns. Over $5 million per month is spent at Moshannon to imprison more than 1,600 people, the majority of whom have NO CRIMINAL CHARGES. Federal law is clear that immigration detention is only for the purpose of ensuring attendance at hearings and for imminent deportation.  Some of those sent to Moshannon were detained when they showed up for their hearings!

The private prison company uses people our government has detained to do most of the labor at the “processing center.” Meanwhile, reports of inadequate food and medical care, sexual harassment, and at least three detainee deaths indicate that the processing center may be violating basic humanitarian standards.

As Members of Congress, we are responsible for conducting oversight to ensure that taxpayer dollars are spent wisely and well.  We also represent constituents (a term that includes all who reside in our districts) who have been detained at Moshannon, and we have a responsibility to ensure their rights are not violated. https://t.co/lUzO8uM10G

239 years later, that lesson still matters.

On Constitution Day, let’s remember what begins the document, and what America has always been about: “We the People.”

text:
Last night, I voted for the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act, legislation I cosponsored, to help protect South Texas families and small businesses from paying the electricity infrastructure costs created by large data centers.

The principle is simple: if a project creates the cost, the project should pay the cost.

Data centers can require new power generation, transmission lines, substations, and other upgrades to the electric grid. This bill would help make sure those costs stay with the large customers that require them instead of being shifted onto families and small businesses. It also includes protections so ratepayers are not left with the bill if a data center later scales back or shuts down.

This is a step in the right direction, but there is more work to do. Data centers also use significant amounts of water and can put additional pressure on local infrastructure. As more of these facilities are built, we need to look at the full impact on the communities where they operate.

South Texas families should not be asked to subsidize massive private projects. I will continue working to protect ratepayers and make sure the companies creating these costs are the ones paying for them.

urls.description: The Constitution is the most sacred document in American history—it's our founding text and guidepost for our laws and society. It was first drafted in 1787 at the Constitutional Convention with the Preamble and seven articles. In 1791, the Bill of Rights were added, consisting of the first 10 amendments.Since 1992, the Constitution has composed of the Preamble, seven articles, and 27 amendments. I'm including it here for your reference.Best,Mike Quigley
urls.title: The United States Constitution | Congressman Mike Quigley

On this day, 239 years ago, the U.S. Constitution was signed, establishing the very foundation of our democracy and the supreme law of the land.

Today, we don’t just celebrate a document. We recognize its promise of freedom and reaffirm our commitment to pursuing a more perfect union.

Happy Constitution Day, America!

text:
Hard-working families in eastern North Carolina deserve a tax system that actually works for them, not one that gives tax advantages to data centers. 

H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, expands tax incentives that can benefit  data centers. That is why Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet and I introduced legislation to exclude data centers from the 100% bonus depreciation deduction and Opportunity Zone tax benefits.

At a time when so many families are struggling with high costs, we are working to ensure federal tax policy reflects the needs of families and communities across eastern North Carolina and our nation.
